text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Norwegian electricity producers say last year's crisis in the electricity market is over. Water reservoir levels are again high enough to secure electricity supply during the winter. Electricity prices rose sharply in 1996 because of a lack of rain.
-Norwegian fishing industry booked revenues of 25 billion crowns last year. Fish sales make up the second largest export industry after oil.

-As many as 40,000 people in Norway should not drive because they are under influence of various medicine. Laws should be changed and drugs should be considered by the same rules as alcohol in traffic, a researcher says.
-Norway's Central Bank announced it was cutting key interest rates, effective from Thursday, to deter the crown from rising, but the currency kept firming.
-The Norwegian all share-index rose above 1,000 points for the first time with blue chips leading the way.
